cases.description: Single-use dispatch admission on two Control processes (SEC-02); since P0.2 also the derived authority (SEC-01): the dispatch owner is the verified caller's workload identity (a forged owner and a wrong workload are PERMISSION_DENIED), an owner reads and reports only its own dispatches and every read is bound to the tenant it acts for. P1 (plan 0002) SEC-02 negative 'same call on two replicas': one admission per command identity on two Control processes.

P0.1 workload identity on Control, Knowledge and MCP: plaintext, a foreign CA, a trusted certificate with a wrong trust domain, one without a URI SAN and an unauthorized workload are refused; the allowed workload reaches the handler. JWT audience, issuer and signature validation is IT-USER-AUTHZ (P0.3).

P0.3 user identity on the development OIDC provider: a token of another audience, of an unmapped user, with a forged signature or none, an expired or tenant-less forgery and an opaque fixture token are refused with WWW-Authenticate; a tenant or actor stated in a request never reaches Control (forged tenant/actor); an unknown action is refused; a user of another project of the same tenant neither reads nor commands the operation while the operator role crosses projects; only a user holding the operator role begins a recovery run. Expiry, issuer, unknown kid and the algorithm allowlist are the verifier's table test (U-API).

P0.4 on a Cilium cluster: stand-in pods carrying each component's labels and ports; every matrix flow connects, every other pair and port is refused (direct Model Proxy, Knowledge, Control or data-store access from a pod the matrix does not name, including an unlabeled pod of anvilkit-apps). Stand-ins, not the deployed services: the services' own traffic under the policies is NR-NETWORK.

Controlled Model Proxy calls through Control and the countable upstream. P1 (plan 0002) SEC-02 negatives: 'hidden transport retry' (P1.1: a 421 is one receive, one dispatch and one send; the platform fetch's re-send is refused before the wire), 'lost grant response' and 'same call on two replicas' (P1.3: a reentry reattaches to the original call, never a second send), 'cancellation race' (cancel and reenter under the original identity; P1.3: a rollout drains a held send).

Ingestion (P15) through the real parser launcher on kind with the parser image of P0.7 (stager in isolated mode, separate /tmp volumes for the stagers and the parser, trixie base without CRITICAL findings): markdown and PDF parsed and accepted with provenance, an archive bomb refused inside the Job, tampered parser Jobs denied at admission with the launcher's own credentials (a /tmp shared by the parser and stage-out among them), the accepted chunks embedded over the HTTPS Inference listener (P0.6, F-P0.1-2).

P2.6: the knowledge journey through the public Agent API alone (nothing written to the bucket by the test): beginSourceUpload, the presigned PUT with exactly the signed headers, registerSource upload:<uploadId>, ingest observed to indexed, createSnapshot, a cited search, a fact citing the source proposed, confirmed and recalled; the capability refused a second time and for another tenant, the snapshot unreadable by another tenant.

Guarded MCP tool execution. P1 (plan 0002) SEC-02 negatives: 'hidden transport retry' (P1.2: HTTP/1.1-only egress, a body-bound failure is never replayed; results the record cannot hold settle FAILED/RESULT_TOO_LARGE), 'lost grant response' (the operator path reconciles one call under its original identity).

The background lane (P14) on a data plane run as the target platform runs it (P0.6): PostgreSQL TLS-only (pg_hba refuses plaintext, every DSN verify-full), NATS TLS-only with one NKey user per role limited to its subjects, Valkey TLS-only with the default user off and one ACL user per role limited to its owner's keys; the services connect with file-based credentials. Negatives: plaintext and anonymous NATS, an unlisted NKey, a forwarder publishing into another owner's subjects, plaintext Valkey, the default user, a wrong password, another owner's keys, a dangerous command, a plaintext or foreign-CA PostgreSQL connection; a Valkey ACL password rotated with two passwords and the worker rolled, the old one refused, Valkey not restarted.

cases.description: P1.5/P1.6 (plan 0002) Control admission path: prepared dispatches denied at attempt close and authorized ones reconciled from their original identity, launch confirmation re-validated under the fence, unique recovery epochs and exclusive scopes, index-served hot paths, bounded finalize memory, counted capacity refusals, and stored settlement intents re-applied once the last obligation resolves. SEC-02 negative 'cancellation race': a fence between the launch record and its confirmation creates no Job.

P1.6 (plan 0002) bounded Workflow histories under long reconciliation (continue-as-new of settlements and recovery rounds), holds that keep accepted stages and Control outages retried rather than reported as budget verdicts. SEC-02 negative 'lost grant response': a refused funding is reported once, an unreachable Control is retried under the same command.

P1.7 (plan 0002) replay of the recorded histories in internal/workflows/testdata/histories (runs before and after the P1.6 version markers) on the current Workflow code; removing a GetVersion guard fails it.

P1.6 (plan 0002) transfer failures without capability material, model-call heartbeats on keepalives, Control status classification (a budget refusal is not retried, capacity is) and the launcher's observation cadence with 200 Jobs.

P1.6/P1.7 (plan 0002) on the foundation's Temporal: no signing parameter, bucket or key in history, logs or spans after a forced transfer failure; the Worker Deployment Versioning upgrade drill (pinned runs finish on their build, new runs land on the current build, no non-determinism).

TEST-05 (P3.4 AC4): migration N+1 (Control 00018) applied to a populated database while image N (the release without its newest migration) serves LocalCheck traffic, then one Control process at N and one at N+1 and a Workflow worker restart with runs in flight: no failed admission, no lock_timeout retry, image N ready on the newer schema, every run succeeded, no non-determinism. The image-rollout half on Kubernetes is TestUpgradeDrill.
P1.4/P1.7 (plan 0002) API stream caps with retryable refusals and readiness, and a drain that ends every open stream with an end event, flushes traces and exits 0.

P3.4: Control's database recovered to a named point before five obligation classes; a new recovery epoch fences the old exits, the inventory is enumerated and every finding reconciled under its original identity before admission reopens (DEVELOPMENT_ONLY placement).
P3.4: Knowledge's database recovered to a point before memory deletions and revocations; every removal is re-applied from the restore-surviving inventory before memory serves.

P3.4 (TEST-02): 2-way and 8-way races of one call identity over two Control processes whose obligation inventory is the foundation's S3 store; exactly one dispatchAllowed=true and one physical send (DEVELOPMENT_ONLY: host processes, MinIO).

P3.4 (EVAL-04): the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY retrieval quality bounds (tests/evals/rag/thresholds.json) accept the recorded development measurements and refuse a degraded recall, a disclosure, an invalid citation and another corpus; TestRetrieval asserts them on every live run.

P3.5 AC4: the IT-MODEL-PROXY intermittent (two observations of one invalid-usage call) reproduced 7/100 and closed: FilesystemStore's conditional put was check-then-act across instances; it now holds the key's lock across the version check and the rename (0/100 since). The forced reclaim-before-settlement cases assert one observation without new evidence and one supplemental observation under a fresh sequence with usage. DEVELOPMENT_ONLY store (the S3 store's If-Match is atomic).

P3.5 AC1/AC5 (G-14 load/capacity): p50/p95 of admission, first progress, end-to-end, SSE recovery, search and catalog latency at the profile's rates, with queue oldest age, relay backlog and Control pool utilization from the metrics stack. The shipped profile is DEVELOPMENT_ONLY until ENV-05 supplies the arrival rates; Preparation and search run only with their tenant inputs.

P3.5 AC2: zero duplicate sends (upstream receives = admitted model dispatches; NOT_MEASURED without a countable upstream), zero duplicate charges, zero operations stuck reconciling, zero SENDER_LOST from rollouts, no container restart from load, every rollout ready.

P3.5 AC3: per fault the designed outcome (readiness drop and return, failover, fenced admission, UNKNOWN then reconciled), no duplicate charge, no dispatch past its deadline unresolved, every accepted operation exists once and ends, no operation with two Jobs.

SEC-09 cluster negatives: each forged image/SA/command/CSI/capability template refused by admission, and exec or ephemeral-container injection refused (RBAC for the launcher, policy for an administrator).
SEC-09/G-13: unsigned, foreign-signed, tagged and foreign-registry images refused by the qualification cluster's admission; a signed release image by digest admitted.

notRun.reason: No qualified provider route, price, quota or cap exists; every model call runs against the countable controlled upstream, so repeated Agent trials with real models (success, all-trial success, cost, latency) cannot run and no quality figure is reported.
No gVisor/Cilium/kernel target runtime: the candidate profiles codegen-fixed-v1 and codegen-team-dev-v1 stay DISABLED on the development foundation.
Pagix source, lease, review, publication and activation ports are the Workflow's DEVELOPMENT_ONLY double; no real idempotency, query or receipt capability is observed.
No qualified Studio host, preview origin or CSP; the certified host ABI (host-abi-dev-v1) is not the Studio host's (studio-host-v1).

Workload mTLS with SPIFFE URI SAN authorization (IT-IDENTITY) and the API's OIDC verification with project/role authorization (IT-USER-AUTHZ) run on the development PKI and the disposable development OIDC provider only (cert-manager self-signed root, trust domain anvilkit.local; deploy/dev/oidc): no production trust material (ENV-03) and no production IdP issuer, audience or claim schema (ENV-07), so neither is qualified.
No HA topology, independent failure domain, PITR or Ceph/RGW inventory; two local processes are not failure-domain evidence.
The RAG and memory cases are DEVELOPMENT_ONLY sets written by the implementing agent, not the approved business-labeled corpus; no quality threshold is derived from them.
Tool execution runs against the official-SDK fixture server behind a disposable ContextForge; no real paid-read or side-effecting upstream is qualified.
No Valkey/NATS/PostgreSQL process-failure drills, Apollo/OpenBao control planes or Temporal SDK upgrade replay on a qualified environment.

Every case runs on the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY foundation (kind, single-node Compose services, Testcontainers); a gate closes only on its entire real-environment evidence in a qualified environment (P23), never on local or synthetic results.
No signed images, SBOMs, published charts, clean install on a target cluster or replacement inventory; the working trees are uncommitted.

No enforcing-CNI environment runs the deployed services: the qualification cluster's kindnet does not enforce NetworkPolicy and the verification RKE2/Cilium environment is not deployed, so the integration scenarios and the LocalCheck probe Job have not run under the policies (P0.4 AC3), and the egress CIDRs of Pagix, providers, MCP upstreams, ContextForge and the inventory are ENV-03 inputs.

On the DEVELOPMENT_ONLY qualification cluster (run 20261010T053549Z, delivery.md P0 close-out) the CSI delivery, the Secret listing (check-secrets.py --cluster: 50 Secrets, 0 findings), drills.py secret-rotation (PASS on the second attempt) and restore-drills.py openbao ran and passed; none ran on a qualified ENV-01 environment, and seal custody (KMS unseal instead of Shamir shares on a workstation) is ENV-10. Since the 2026-10-13 host restart the qualification OpenBao is sealed and awaits an authorized unseal.

scenarios.M1-01: Duplicate submission, cross-tenant observation, reconnect and cancellation

scenarios.M1-05: Independent certification rejects fake exit code, missing CSS and wrong ABI
scenarios.M1-06: Any subject-field change invalidates prior approval
scenarios.M1-07: npm succeeds while browser target is unknown: query original identity only
scenarios.M1-08: Activate only when both receipts and approval match
scenarios.M1-09: Load a new remote component without rebuilding host; reject name collision
scenarios.M1-10: Exact old-page version; unavailable-component placeholder preserves props
scenarios.M1-11: Aggregate role costs; separate credits and actual cost; clocks never reset
scenarios.M1-12: Enumerate unknown external obligations after database rollback
scenarios.M1-14: Supported commands respect definition revision/fence; stale commands cannot reverse newer state
scenarios.M1-15: Structured brief; every analysis call independently controlled
scenarios.M1-16: Grouped two rounds/three questions, original seven-day clock, duplicate Update
scenarios.M1-17: Exact source/brand/material hashes and current ACL
scenarios.CAP-01: Bounded multi-Agent team (fixed roles, bounded parallelism, one writer, combined budget, accepted-stage recovery, independent certification)
scenarios.CAP-02: RAG and vectors (ingestion, isolated parsing, dense/sparse, rerank, citations, current ACL, generations, labeled set)
scenarios.CAP-04: MCP marketplace and effects (discovery, review, grants, pinned protocol, real execution, uncertain effects)
scenarios.CAP-05: Background queues and event bus (reconstructible BullMQ, NATS outbox/inbox, duplicate/out-of-order recovery)
scenarios.CAP-06: Fx and configuration lifecycle (typed snapshots, validated replacement, secret rotation, bounded shutdown)
scenarios.CAP-07: Complete replacement and Kubernetes deployment (independent workloads, failure domains, backups, telemetry, supply chain)
scenarios.SEC-01: Forged tenant/actor or workload impersonation: cross-tenant request, wrong SAN/audience, expired evidence, unknown action
scenarios.SEC-02: Duplicate charges: same call on two replicas, lost grant response, cancellation race, summary bypass
scenarios.SEC-03: Candidate steals keys or forges results: secret reads, trusted-socket access, verdict tampering, PID/fd transfer
scenarios.SEC-04: Same-Pod network bypass: AF_INET, IPv6, localhost, metadata, direct Proxy/Knowledge access
scenarios.SEC-05: Cross-tenant/revoked RAG disclosure: sparse branch leakage, old snapshots, revocation race, hit-count leakage
scenarios.SEC-06: Memory poisoning: model self-confirmation, cross-subject writes, out-of-order upsert, recall after deletion
scenarios.SEC-07: MCP SSRF/credential forwarding: discovery/redirect/JWKS metadata, DNS rebinding, cross-host authorization
scenarios.SEC-08: Tool substitution or revocation race: schema mutation, old grant, calls around revoke response, in-flight calls
scenarios.SEC-09: Launcher privilege expansion: forged image/SA/command/CSI/capabilities, exec or ephemeral-container injection
scenarios.SEC-10: Malicious PDF/archive/source dependency: archive bomb, path/symlink escape, plugin download, candidate build configuration
scenarios.SEC-11: Rollback revives send rights: truncated listing, omitted call after restore, old token, partial storage failure
scenarios.SEC-12: Page imports unapproved/wrong component: old lock replaced by latest, type collision, discarded unknown props, weakened CSP
